candidates.source_name: Euronet Slovakia (euronet.sk) – independent ATM deployer corporate site
candidates.why_relevant: Euronet is the largest non-bank (IAD) ATM deployer in SK; its own site carries network positioning, fee/DCC terms, ATM locator and outsourcing offers to banks/retailers — the primary window into the non-bank ATM buying layer.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: periodic HTML fetch of /o-nas, /kontakt and ATM locator pages; diff for network/service changes
queries_used: Euronet bankomaty Slovensko sieť prevádzkovateľ počet

candidates.source_name: Euronet ATM Solutions (euronetatms.com) – outsourcing/ATM-as-a-service product site
candidates.why_relevant: Group-level product/solution pages (ATM outsourcing, CIT ATMs, branch automation) show what Euronet sells to banks and retailers across CEE, i.e. the competitive offer set facing hardware/managed-service vendors in SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: crawl /products/* and any case-study/news sections; watch for SK/CEE references
queries_used: Euronet bankomaty Slovensko sieť prevádzkovateľ počet

candidates.source_name: Loomis SK – cash-in-transit and ATM management (sk.loomis.com / loomis.sk)
candidates.why_relevant: Loomis SK runs CIT, cash processing under NBS licence and ATM replenishment/first-line ATM management for SK banks; its product and branch pages map the cash-cycle service layer and identify who actually touches ATM/recycler estates.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: fetch product pages (cash-management, cash-transportation, atm-solutions, protecting-valuables) + about/branch pages; also monitor legacy domain loomis.sk
queries_used: Loomis Slovakia preprava hotovosti spracovanie hotovosti banka

candidates.source_name: G4S / Securitas Slovakia – security and cash services presence pages
candidates.why_relevant: G4S Security Services (SK) is described as the largest private security provider in SK and includes money transport; establishes the second CIT pole alongside Loomis and the Securitas-group ownership overlay.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: fetch SK country pages; cross-check legal entities (G4S Security Services (SK) a.s., G4S Secure Solutions (SK) s.r.o.) in ORSR/FinStat
queries_used: Brink's Slovensko G4S Cash Services Securitas preprava peňazí spoločnosť

candidates.source_name: Brink's Czech/CEE cash solutions site (brinks.cz) – regional CIT reference
candidates.why_relevant: No distinct SK Brink's site surfaced; the CZ entity documents the CEE CIT lineage (Group 4 Securitas → G4S Cash Services → Brink's) and partnerships that shape the neighbouring/cross-border cash-handling market relevant to SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: monitor /novinky-a-blogy for CEE contract and partnership announcements; treat SK relevance as inferential
queries_used: Brink's Slovensko G4S Cash Services Securitas preprava peňazí spoločnosť

candidates.source_name: COOP Jednota Slovensko – COOP miniBANKOMAT / CashBack service pages
candidates.why_relevant: COOP Jednota runs the largest retail cash-at-checkout network in SK (~2,000 stores, limit raised to EUR 100, partner banks UniCredit, ČSOB, SLSP, 365.bank) — the clearest evidence of retail as a cash-access channel competing with ATMs, plus named bank/scheme partnerships.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: fetch service pages and the /files/media/documents press-release PDFs; also poll regional COOP Jednota sites (Galanta, Poprad) for local rollout detail
queries_used: COOP Jednota Slovnaft cashback výber hotovosti pri pokladni obchod

candidates.source_name: Lidl Slovenská republika – corporate press room (spolocnost.lidl.sk)
candidates.why_relevant: Lidl SK announces checkout technology rollouts (self-checkout, e-labels) in its own press releases — a primary record of self-service checkout deployment volumes and timing at the largest discounter.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: scrape the tlačové správy archive by year; keyword filter samoobslužné pokladnice / platba / technológie
queries_used: samoobslužné pokladne Lidl Tesco Kaufland Slovensko nasadenie dodávateľ

candidates.source_name: Forbes.sk – retail technology / self-checkout coverage
candidates.why_relevant: Business media aggregate self-checkout counts across chains (Lidl, Kaufland, Tesco ~half of transactions, Billa 52 stores) that retailers do not publish uniformly — the best cross-chain deployment benchmark found.

candidates.why_relevant: DPB is the buyer of Bratislava's open-loop contactless ticketing ('Kartuj', succeeded by 'Tapni sa'); its news section documents launch dates, accepted schemes and on-board validator changes — a direct transit-payments buyer record.

candidates.source_name: ÚVO – Vestník verejného obstarávania and contract search
candidates.why_relevant: The statutory tender bulletin is the single richest pointer for the non-bank buyer layer: transport operators, Slovenská pošta, municipalities and state retailers must publish notices and awards there, exposing incumbent suppliers and contract values for ATMs, validators, POS and cash services.
candidates.access_status: open web; JS-driven search UI, below-threshold contracts (<EUR 50k) excluded
candidates.suggested_collection_method: structured keyword queries (bankomat, platobný terminál, validátor, preprava hotovosti, samoobslužná pokladňa) against the notices search and profiles; consider EPVO portal for live tenders

brief: Slovakia's non-bank cash and self-service buyer layer is documented across four distinct source families: operator/vendor sites (Euronet SK, Loomis SK, G4S/Securitas SK), retailer service and newsroom pages (COOP Jednota's miniBANKOMAT/cashback network of ~2,000 stores, Lidl SK press releases on self-checkout), public-sector procurement records for transport and postal buyers (DPMK Košice's own verejné obstarávanie and contract register, DPB news, ÚVO's Vestník), and statistical/regulatory anchors at NBS and the SBA. The sharpest asymmetry is disclosure regime: transport operators and Slovenská pošta leave a full tender trail naming suppliers and values, while private retail chains publish deployment counts but never vendors — so retail self-checkout and terminal suppliers will have to be inferred from trade press, job ads and integrator references. Community documentation (imhd.sk) is unusually valuable for fare-technology history in Bratislava and Košice and should be treated as a lead generator to be corroborated, not as a primary. Key open items are the SK-specific size of Euronet's ATM estate, the supplier chain behind Bratislava's open-loop 'Tapni sa' ticketing, and the entirely unscouted petrol-network segment.
